about.title: about me
about.p1: I grew up in Chile and moved to France at 27, without any big reason: I just wanted to start a new life.
about.p2: I don’t believe in fixed identities, which may explain my multidisciplinary path. I’m transmasc and I love it. I studied theater; steady gigs were rare, but I never stopped creating.
about.p3: In France I became a sound technician for concerts, film and exhibitions. Then I trained as a full-stack developer at Ada Tech School. And here I am, making a life out of all of them :)
about.portraitAlt: Gabriel in profile, in a dark sweater, behind a texture of gray and violet scan lines.

metadata.title: Web development · Gabriel Hono
metadata.description: Gabriel Hono’s web development work: full-stack projects in TypeScript, React and Next.js.

journey.title: my journey
journey.text: I came to code in a funny way. In France I kept meeting people who worked in tech, and I never understood what they did. They explained, I nodded, and I had no idea what they meant when they said “HTML”. When I decided to retrain, I realized how fascinating code is, and how close it is to the creative work I love: you build something, test it, rework it until it holds, just like in rehearsal. It’s creation, technique and a constant intellectual challenge, and I’m someone who loves learning something new every day.

metadata.title: Theater and performance · Gabriel Hono
metadata.description: Gabriel Hono’s theater and performance work in Chile: directing, acting, producing and a site-specific sound walk.

journey.title: my journey
journey.p1: I studied theater at Universidad Mayor in Santiago, from 2013 to 2016. I was trained as an actor, but I never really felt like one, so I started exploring directing. After drama school I directed <cite>Animales binarios</cite> and <cite>Pero, ¿y mi madre?</cite>, and was assistant director on <cite>Todo bajo control</cite>.
journey.p2: From 2020 to 2022, I did a master’s in theater studies and practices at the Universidad Católica de Chile, researching the ethical relationship between artist and audience. What I look for on stage is truth: no pretending, only what is really happening in the present. That took me from plays to performance, starting from the most intimate place so it can resonate with each spectator’s own story.
journey.p3: I also learned to run projects: I produced the <cite>Juan Radrigán</cite> inter-school playwriting festival from 2015 to 2018, and for <cite>Caminamos mirando al cielo</cite>, a sound walk made during the pandemic, I wrote my first application to Fondart, Chile’s national arts fund, and won it. And I taught, as a teaching assistant in directing at Universidad Mayor and in applied theater at the UC. When I moved to France, I stepped away from the stage, but not from creating.

metadata.title: Sound · Gabriel Hono
metadata.description: Gabriel Hono’s sound work in France: location recording and mixing for film, live sound for concerts and sound art installations.

journey.title: my journey
journey.p1: Sound came to me through performance: during the pandemic, with no bodies allowed on stage, it was the only way I found to reach an audience.
journey.p2: In France I trained as a sound technician at CIFACOM (BTS Audiovisuel, 2023–2025): choosing microphones, location recording, mixing. Along the way, I’ve recorded and mixed short films, assisted on live sound for an open-air opera festival, installed sound artworks in a gallery, and I now work concerts with Orchestre Hélios in Paris churches.

mapiscine.title: MaPiscine
mapiscine.description: A web app that brings together the information on Paris’s 42 municipal swimming pools. Interactive map and list, with filters for wheelchair access, a Queer Friendly label, payment methods and live opening status. With an account, users can save favorites and leave reviews.
mapiscine.role: Solo project: design and development, from user research to deployment

s1.title: Why.
s1.body: Information on Paris pools is scattered across dozens of pages and hard to compare. As a queer person, I also wanted to know in advance how welcoming a pool would be.

s2.title: Process.
s2.body: I ran it solo from start to finish: personas, wireframes in Excalidraw, Figma mockups, a relational data model, then development, 23 unit tests and continuous deployment.

s3.title: A technical challenge.
s3.body: Next.js runs the proxy in the Edge Runtime, where Prisma can’t work. I moved session checks to an internal API route running on Node: the proxy calls it, then passes the user’s ID and role to the route handlers.

s4.title: Next steps.
s4.body: The admin backend is built and tested; its interface is next, along with holiday opening hours. I’d like to partner with the pools and Paris queer associations, so the data and the Queer Friendly label are kept up to date by those who know them best.

cityson.title: CitySon
cityson.description: A sound map of Paris: each pin holds an audio piece tied to a precise place, meant to be heard on site. Designed for site-specific sound art and performance, it could also work as a social network for located sounds. Prototype: the map and the pieces are live; posting is in progress.
cityson.role: Solo project: concept, design and development

s1.title: Where it comes from.
s1.body: Between 2020 and 2022 in Chile, I created <cite>Caminamos mirando al cielo</cite>, a site-specific sound walk: listeners had to reach a precise spot, and then the audio guided them. The hardest part was explaining to people how to take part. CitySon is the tool I wish I’d had.

s2.title: What it does.
s2.body: Anyone, artists first, can pin a sound to a place on the map. To hear it as intended, you go there: listening becomes situated.

s3.title: How it’s built.
s3.body: A React front end and an Express REST API over PostgreSQL, deployed separately. A prototype built in two weeks: today you can explore the map and open each piece.

s4.title: Next steps.
s4.body: Posting sounds, authentication and favorites, then a React Native version: it’s an app meant to be used while walking through the city.

caminamos.title: Caminamos mirando al cielo
caminamos.translatedTitle: We walk looking at the sky
caminamos.place: Costanera Center, Santiago. Master’s final project (UC). Process exhibition at Teatro del Puente. Funded by Fondart.
caminamos.hover: A one-hour sound walk through a Santiago mall, about memory and mental health.
caminamos.popup: Listeners signed up, stood outside the Costanera Center and pressed play on their own phone. For an hour, a voice guided them through the mall’s five floors, asking them to walk, touch, clap, take photos. The building is known for the people who have died there by suicide: the piece invites you to walk it as a place of memory, and shares mental-health information and where to find help. Loosely inspired by Greek myths (Odysseus, Narcissus, Pandora, Hestia).
caminamos.credits: Creation and direction: Gabriel Hono · Dramaturgy: Nicolás Lange and Gabriel Hono · Voices: Gabriel Hono, Javiera Mendoza, Consuelo Carreño, Beatriz Arredondo · Sound composition and editing: Juanjo Acuña · Photos: Manuela Bocaz

animales-binarios.title: Animales binarios
animales-binarios.hover: Three characters dissect the childhood that still lives in their queer bodies.
animales-binarios.popup: Three intertwined monologues by playwright Carla Fuentes Abu-Abbarah: three queer characters with a shared past revisit their childhood, its abuse and its loneliness, looking for a way out. I directed the piece and led the project as a whole, from building the team to finding the funding. It ran for 32 performances between October 2017 and mid-2018.

todo-bajo-control.title: Todo bajo control
todo-bajo-control.place: Santiago de Chile, in several theaters over three years of touring
todo-bajo-control.hover: Christmas Eve, a strike, and five supermarket cashiers trying to save their holidays.
todo-bajo-control.popup: Five cashiers at a supermarket in an upscale Santiago neighborhood face Christmas Eve and a workers’ strike at the same time. How far would you go to save Christmas? Do you work to live, or live to work? Written by Javiera Mendoza and directed by Juan Gálvez, the play won the drama school’s internal creation fund, then toured Santiago theaters until 2019. I was assistant director.

pero-y-mi-madre.title: Pero, ¿y mi madre?
pero-y-mi-madre.place: La Máquina del Arte, Santiago de Chile
pero-y-mi-madre.hover: A couple travels through a dream without leaving their bedroom.
pero-y-mi-madre.popup: A comedy by Carmen Amador, who started writing under Juan Radrigán’s mentorship, about identity as something built through our relationships. Sol and Fede set out on a journey of self-discovery without leaving their room: in a dream, they are visited by the ghosts of their parents, and even by their own older selves. The bedroom, where we are most honestly ourselves, slowly turns into a dream (or a nightmare) that the audience witnesses.
pero-y-mi-madre.credits: Text: Carmen Amador · Direction: Gabriel Hono · Assistant: Nicolás Pérez · Production: Beatriz Arredondo · Cast: Manuel Almonacid, Beatriz Arredondo, Diego Sánchez, Carmen Peñailillo

festival-juan-radrigan.title: Festival de Dramaturgia Interescuelas Juan Radrigán
festival-juan-radrigan.place: Universidad Mayor drama school, Santiago de Chile
festival-juan-radrigan.hover: A student playwriting festival that grew from 10 to 70 submissions.
festival-juan-radrigan.popup: An inter-school playwriting festival for drama students, named after Chilean playwright Juan Radrigán. I joined its production team for the second edition. As a new team, we brought in experienced theater professionals, raised the prizes, looked for more funding and built collaborations between drama schools. Submissions grew from 10 texts in the first edition to 70 in my last one, and the drama school’s support grew every year, funding staged readings, guest artists and the award ceremony. The festival is now in its twelfth year, still on the course we set.

la-methode.title: La Méthode
la-methode.role: Production sound mixer and re-recording mixer; music recording
la-methode.place: Short fiction, BTS final project, CIFACOM, Paris
la-methode.hover: A drama student, a monologue, and a blurred line between fiction and reality.
la-methode.popup: A short fiction about a drama student struggling with a monologue, playing with the line between reality and fiction. I recorded sound over three shooting days (an apartment, a park, a studio), then edited and mixed the film to broadcast delivery standards. I also art-directed and recorded the original score for viola da gamba, composed and played by Lukas Carrillo, combining a close and a distant microphone to capture both detail and depth.

andi.title: ANDI
andi.role: Writer, director, sound recordist and mixer
andi.hover: A documentary portrait built on one intimate interview.
andi.popup: A short documentary exploring Andi’s experience and identity through an intimate interview. I wrote and directed it, recorded the sound and mixed it. The challenge was an 11 m² room with heavy reverb: a boom and a lavalier mic on set, room tone recorded for post, then noise cleanup, phase alignment, EQ and a light reverb in Pro Tools. No music, no added ambiences: just Andi’s voice.
andi.credits: Writing, direction and sound: Gabriel Hono · Camera: Camille Konnert, Marco Tafolla · Editing: Zoé Perrier · Production: Lola Brisset, Abel Lukoki · Photos: Camille Konnert

les-arenes-lyriques.title: Les Arènes Lyriques
les-arenes-lyriques.place: Open-air classical and opera festival, Arènes de Montmartre, Paris
les-arenes-lyriques.hover: Four weeks of open-air opera sound in Montmartre.
les-arenes-lyriques.popup: An open-air classical and opera festival in the Arènes de Montmartre. As assistant to sound engineer Zéphir Torres, I helped position and angle the PA, set the delay for the rear speakers, install the digital console, stage rack, amplifiers and wireless systems, then cable and line-check before every concert. Being outdoors, we often had to cover or strip everything down when rain came: four weeks that taught me how fast live sound has to adapt.
les-arenes-lyriques.credits: Festival director: Pierre Mollaret · Sound engineer: Zéphir Torres · Night photo: Les Arènes Lyriques

tuning-of-the-afterworld.title: The Tuning of the Afterworld
tuning-of-the-afterworld.place: Sound art exhibition, La Box gallery, ENSA Bourges
tuning-of-the-afterworld.hover: Helping sound artworks find their voice in a gallery.
tuning-of-the-afterworld.popup: A sound art exhibition at La Box, the gallery of the Bourges national art school. I assisted with the installation of the works: wiring the motors, programmable boards and MIDI control of Roxane Marquant’s kinetic objects, placing the pieces of Sonia Saroya and Édouard Sufrin’s <cite>Derniers Souffles</cite>, and watching Basile Richon assemble <cite>Réminiscence d’une mer</cite>, which turns tides engraved on aluminum discs into sound. It showed me sound as a sculptural material, far from film and concerts.
tuning-of-the-afterworld.credits: Curator: Fanny Testas · Artists: Roxane Marquant, Basile Richon, Sonia Saroya, Édouard Sufrin
